original_value: SMART-based NoC designs achieve ultra-low latencies by enabling flits to traverse multiple hops within a single clock cycle. Notwithstanding the clear performance benefits, SMART-based NoCs suffer from several shortcomings: each router must arbitrate among a quadratic number of requests, which leads to high costs; each router independently makes its own arbitration decisions, which leads to a problem called false negatives that causes throughput loss. In this article, we propose a new SMART-based NoC design called SHARP that overcomes these shortcomings. Our evaluation demonstrates that SHARP increases throughput by up to 19% and average link utilization by up to 24% by avoiding false negatives. By avoiding quadratic arbitration, our evaluation further demonstrates that SHARP reduces the wiring and area overhead significantly.

result.paraphrase: SMART-based NoC architectures deliver ultra-low latency by letting flits cross multiple hops in a single clock cycle. However, these networks have several drawbacks: every router has to arbitrate among a quadratic number of requests, driving up cost; and because each router arbitrates independently, false negatives can occur, reducing throughput. In this paper, we introduce SHARP, a new SMART-based NoC design that addresses these issues. Our evaluation shows that, by eliminating false negatives, SHARP boosts throughput by as much as 19% and raises average link utilization by up to 24%. It also significantly lowers wiring and area overhead by avoiding quadratic arbitration.
